parsed.reason: The plan is grounded in the playbook and a parent could start it tonight. It names the method (iron-first, then allergens early and often) with a one-line why (Health Canada/CPS, LEAP ~80%). Stages follow the playbook: Day 1, Days 2-7, Week 2 peanut (half a teaspoon thinned, taste, 10-minute wait, 2-hour watch, no other new foods), then egg and the rest, one a day. It keeps the twice-weekly rotation and says no testing is needed first. It uses the playbook's allergen list with no US big-9 framing and no invented spacing. Safety content is accurate: gagging versus silent choking, the 911 triggers, stop-and-see-provider for mild reactions, eczema check, no honey, no whole nuts. There is a check-in day (Thursday) and a non-guaranteeing tone. Weaknesses: it is a little compressed. Choking is conflated with 911 in one clause. It omits baby-led weaning as a named alternative, the 9-month lumpy texture milestone, and the readiness signs. It lacks an explicit 'how to tell it's working' beyond the expectations, and it leaves out the playbook's refusal reassurance (try again). The 'half teaspoon' is playbook-sourced, so it is not an invented dose. Overall it is strong but not complete.
